title: Azure Bastion Session Audit

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.54 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.54 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="BastionAuditLogs"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.54_azure_bastion_session_au_54"
| sort -_time
description: Bastion provides secure, auditable VM access without public IPs. Monitoring session activity ensures compliance with access policies and detects unauthorized connection attempts.
value: Detecting azure bastion session audit early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable diagnostic logging on Azure Bastion to send audit logs via Event Hub. Track user sessions by `userName`, `targetVMIPAddress`, `protocol` (SSH/RDP), and `duration`. Alert on connections to unexpected VMs, connections from unusual IP addresses, and failed authentication attempts. Correlate with Entra ID sign-in logs for identity context.
visualization: Table (sessions by user and target), Bar chart (sessions by protocol), Line chart (session count over time).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable diagnostic logging on Azure Bastion to send audit logs via Event Hub. Track user sessions by `userName`, `targetVMIPAddress`, `protocol` (SSH/RDP), and `duration`. Alert on connections to unexpected VMs, connections from unusual IP addresses, and failed authentication attempts. Correlate with Entra ID sign-in logs for identity context.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="BastionAuditLogs"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.54_azure_bastion_session_au_54"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:diagnostics` in `index=cloud` to detect azure bastion session audit. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_54_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (sessions by user and target), Bar chart (sessions by protocol), Line chart (session count over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure bastion session audit so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
